conveniencia: Remote backend contract: kara-vfs foundation (Location, RemotePath, Backend trait, WriteSession, BackendError, Capabilities, MemoryBackend, conformance suite)

contrato.resumen: New crate kara-vfs: the protocol-free foundation every remote drive plugs into. It fixes the vocabulary (RemotePath, DriveId, Location with a lossless string URI), the blocking Backend trait with a commit/abort WriteSession that never exposes a half-written file under its final name, a closed BackendError kind set that always names the path, the Capabilities flags the UI reads instead of branching on protocol, an in-memory backend with an SFTP-like and an S3-like profile plus fault injection, and a generic conformance suite that returns a report (never panics) and refuses to run on a non-empty scratch directory. No protocol code, no change to any existing crate except the workspace manifest.

decisionesDeArquitecto.conflicto: docs/remote-backends.md l. 26 puts `MemoryBackend (tests)` in kara-remote; l. 169 (Order of work step 1) and this task's title put it in kara-vfs.
decisionesDeArquitecto.decision: kara-vfs, module `memory`, behind cargo feature `memory`. kara-remote is NOT created in this step. Reason: the conformance suite must be proven against a backend in the same step, and a kara-vfs -> kara-remote dev-dependency would be a cycle once kara-remote depends on kara-vfs.

decisionesDeArquitecto.conflicto: The doc signature is `fn abort(self: Box<Self>);` (l. 76). CLAUDE.md: «Cada syscall devuelve `Result` y cada error se propaga o se reporta». A failed SFTP temp-file cleanup would otherwise be swallowed.
decisionesDeArquitecto.decision: `fn abort(self: Box<Self>) -> Result<(), BackendError>`. Dropping without finish/abort still aborts best-effort (Drop cannot return an error); that path is documented as the only place a cleanup failure is not reported.

decisionesDeArquitecto.conflicto: Location::Remote { drive, path } (l. 34-37) carries no protocol, but the URI form is `kara+sftp://drive-id/…` (l. 45) and must be produced and parsed in Rust with no registry (the registry is step 4).
decisionesDeArquitecto.decision: DriveId carries its scheme: `DriveId { scheme, name }` (both validated). The `Location` enum keeps exactly the two variants of the doc. A drive never changes kind, so the scheme is part of its identity.

decisionesDeArquitecto.conflicto: kara-index already has `Cancel(Arc<AtomicBool>)`, but the doc's layering (l. 19) puts kara-index ABOVE kara-vfs, so kara-vfs cannot import it.
decisionesDeArquitecto.decision: kara-vfs defines `Cancel` with the same semantics (Clone shares state, cancel() idempotent, Relaxed ordering is enough). kara-index is NOT touched in this step; unifying the two is step 3's job.

decisionesDeArquitecto.tema: Error kinds outside the doc's nine
decisionesDeArquitecto.conflicto: The doc's kind list (l. 87-89) has no NotEmpty / NotADirectory / InvalidInput.
decisionesDeArquitecto.decision: The nine kinds stay closed and exhaustive (no #[non_exhaustive]: adding a kind must force kara-ops to update its mapping). Conditions without a kind of their own are `Other` with an `std::io::Error` source of the precise `io::ErrorKind` (DirectoryNotEmpty, NotADirectory, IsADirectory, InvalidInput), so kara-ops can still tell them apart by downcast.

decisionesDeArquitecto.conflicto: The doc puts the suite behind feature `conformance` (l. 24); CLAUDE.md's verification command is plain `cargo test`, which would silently skip feature-gated tests.
decisionesDeArquitecto.decision: Features `memory` and `conformance`, neither in `default`. kara-vfs lists itself as a dev-dependency with both features (`kara-vfs = { path = ".", features = ["memory", "conformance"] }`), so `cargo test -p kara-vfs` and workspace `cargo test` run the suite without flags.

apiPublica.nota: Normative signatures. Names, parameter types and return types are part of the contract. Every public type derives Debug. Everything below is re-exported at the crate root (kara_vfs::RemotePath, kara_vfs::Backend, …) except the memory and conformance modules, reached as kara_vfs::memory::* and kara_vfs::conformance::*.

firmas: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)] pub struct RemotePath(/* private: normalised String */);

impl RemotePath { pub fn root() -> RemotePath; pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<RemotePath, RemotePathError>; pub fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<RemotePath, RemotePathError>; pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str; pub fn is_root(&self) -> bool; pub fn parent(&self) -> Option<RemotePath>; pub fn file_name(&self) -> Option<&str>; pub fn join(&self, segment: &str) -> Result<RemotePath, RemotePathError>; pub fn segments(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str>; pub fn starts_with(&self, base: &RemotePath) -> bool; }
impl std::fmt::Display for RemotePath  // writes as_str()
impl std::str::FromStr for RemotePath { type Err = RemotePathError; }  // same as parse

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)] pub enum RemotePathError { Empty, NotAbsolute { raw: String }, DotSegment { raw: String }, ContainsNul, NotUtf8, InvalidSegment { segment: String } }
items.notas: Canonical form: starts with '/', segments separated by exactly one '/', no trailing '/' except the root "/", no '.' or '..' segment, no NUL, valid UTF-8. parse() collapses repeated '/' and strips a trailing '/'; it REJECTS '.' and '..' instead of resolving them (S3 keys have no such semantics, l. 40-41). No Unicode normalisation. join() takes exactly one segment.

firmas: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)] pub struct DriveId { /* private: scheme: String, name: String */ }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)] pub enum DriveIdError { InvalidScheme { raw: String }, InvalidName { raw: String } }
items.notas: scheme: ASCII, matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,15}$ ("sftp", "s3", "mem"). name: ASCII, matches ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ (a DNS label), so it is a URI authority with no escaping. Equality includes the scheme.

impl Location { pub fn to_uri(&self) -> Result<String, LocationError>; pub fn from_uri(uri: &str) -> Result<Location, LocationError>; pub fn is_local(&self) -> bool; pub fn drive(&self) -> Option<&DriveId>; pub fn same_remote_drive(&self, other: &Location) -> bool; pub fn parent(&self) -> Option<Location>; }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)] pub enum LocationError { RelativeLocalPath, UnsupportedScheme { raw: String }, NonLocalFileHost { host: String }, QueryOrFragment, InvalidPercentEncoding, ContainsNul, Drive(#[from] DriveIdError), Path(#[from] RemotePathError) }
items.notas: Local URI: "file://" + percent-encoded raw bytes of the path (OsStrExt::as_bytes, never lossy), escape set = ASCII controls + space " # % < > ? [ \ ] ^ ` { | } + every byte >= 0x80, uppercase hex — the exact set of crates/kara-fs/src/uri.rs, duplicated (kara-vfs cannot depend on kara-fs). Remote URI: "kara+" + scheme + "://" + name + percent-encoded UTF-8 of path.as_str() with the same escape set. from_uri: lowercase schemes only; "file" requires an empty host; "kara+<scheme>" requires a valid DriveId; a missing path after the authority means root. same_remote_drive is true iff both are Remote with equal DriveId (Local vs Local is false: route 1 is decided elsewhere). parent(): Local uses Path::parent; Remote uses RemotePath::parent on the same drive; roots return None.

firmas: pub trait WriteSession: std::io::Write + Send {
fn finish(self: Box<Self>) -> Result<(), BackendError>;
fn abort(self: Box<Self>) -> Result<(), BackendError>;
items.notas: See dec_02 for abort's return type. Write::flush never commits. Drop without finish/abort aborts best-effort. After any Write::write/flush error, the session is poisoned: finish returns Err (same kind as the first error) and commits nothing.

items.notas: posix_like() capabilities = SFTP column: {trash:false, atomic_rename:true, server_side_copy:false, real_directories:true, posix_permissions:true, symlinks:true, watch:false, undo_rename:true, undo_move:true}. object_store_like() = S3 column: {trash:false, atomic_rename:false, server_side_copy:true, real_directories:false, posix_permissions:false, symlinks:false, watch:false, undo_rename:false, undo_move:false}. with_capabilities makes the BEHAVIOUR follow real_directories, atomic_rename, server_side_copy and symlinks. Fault: `path: None` matches any path; `after` = entries yielded (List), bytes transferred (Read/Write), objects processed (Rename/RemoveTree), ignored otherwise; `times: None` fires until clear_faults. MemorySnapshot holds committed state only (MemoryNode excludes modified times so snapshots compare by value); `nodes` never contains the root. stats counts bytes moved through open_read readers and WriteSession::write, NOT by copy_within. create_symlink returns Unsupported when !capabilities().symlinks. A DirMarker is the object-store `key/` marker (l. 104).

firmas: pub fn run(backend: &dyn Backend, scratch: &RemotePath) -> Result<ConformanceReport, ConformanceError>;
pub const CASE_IDS: &[&str];
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct ConformanceReport { pub cases: Vec<CaseResult> }
impl ConformanceReport { pub fn is_success(&self) -> bool; pub fn failures(&self) -> Vec<&CaseResult>; }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct CaseResult { pub id: &'static str, pub outcome: CaseOutcome }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum CaseOutcome { Passed, Failed { detail: String }, Skipped { because: &'static str } }
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)] pub enum ConformanceError { ScratchUnreachable(#[source] BackendError), ScratchNotDirectory, ScratchNotEmpty { entries: usize } }
items.notas: One generic function, run against every backend (l. 152). It never panics: a backend that misbehaves yields CaseOutcome::Failed with a detail naming the path and what was expected vs observed. CASE_IDS is the normative list below (casosDeConformidad); report.cases has one entry per id, in CASE_IDS order. is_success() == no Failed (Skipped is allowed). `because` is the exact capability condition that caused the skip, e.g. "server_side_copy=false".

casosDeConformidad.nota: Ids of conformance::CASE_IDS, in order. Each runs inside its own fresh subdirectory of `scratch` and removes it at the end (also on failure, best effort). `skipIf` is the ONLY reason a case may be Skipped. Symlink behaviour is not in the generic suite: the trait has no operation to create a link, so it cannot be set up generically; MemoryBackend covers it in cb_39.

rename onto an existing file -> AlreadyExists with path == to; both contents unchanged
rename(x, x) -> Ok, content unchanged
rename(d, d/sub/d2) -> Err (Other), tree unchanged
remove of a file and of an empty dir -> Ok, both NotFound afterwards
remove of a non-empty dir -> Err (Other), nothing removed
remove of a missing path -> NotFound
remove_tree of a 3-level tree -> Ok and the root NotFound; remove_tree of a single file -> Ok
remove_tree with a cancelled Cancel -> Err(Cancelled) and nothing removed
every Err produced by the cases above with a path argument has path == Some(the involved path) per cb_12
capabilities() called before and after all mutations returns equal values
copy_within file -> both readable, identical; onto existing -> AlreadyExists, target unchanged; dir source -> Unsupported
real_directories=false: removing the last object under a prefix with no marker makes the prefix NotFound and absent from list(parent)

casosBorde.titulo: RemotePath canonical form
casosBorde.cita: «`RemotePath`: normalised, `/`-separated, no `.`/`..`, UTF-8.» (remote-backends.md l. 40)
casosBorde.comportamiento: parse collapses repeated '/' and strips one or more trailing '/'; root is exactly "/".
casosBorde.verificable: parse("/a//b/").as_str() == "/a/b"; parse("///") == RemotePath::root(); parse("/").is_root(); parse("/a/b") == parse("/a//b//").

casosBorde.titulo: RemotePath rejections, each with its own variant
casosBorde.cita: «no `.`/`..`, UTF-8. Not a `PathBuf`: S3 keys are not filesystem paths and must not inherit their semantics.» (l. 40-41)
casosBorde.comportamiento: Rejected, not repaired: empty, relative, any '.' or '..' segment (not resolved), NUL, non-UTF-8 bytes.
casosBorde.verificable: parse("") == Err(Empty); parse("a/b") == Err(NotAbsolute{..}); parse("/a/./b") and parse("/a/../b") and parse("/..") == Err(DotSegment{..}); parse("/a\0b") == Err(ContainsNul); from_bytes(b"/a/\xff") == Err(NotUtf8). "/a/..." and "/.hidden" and "/a..b" are VALID (only exact '.'/'..' segments are rejected).

casosBorde.titulo: Unusual but legal characters are kept verbatim; no Unicode normalisation
casosBorde.cita: «list / stat round trip, names with spaces, unicode and `#`/`%`/`?`» (l. 154)
casosBorde.comportamiento: Space, '#', '%', '?', '[', ']', '\\', ':', '*', control characters other than NUL, and any Unicode are ordinary segment characters. NFC and NFD forms of the same text are different paths.
casosBorde.verificable: parse("/a b/#%?\\x").as_str() unchanged and segments() == ["a b", "#%?\\x"]; parse("/caf\u{e9}") != parse("/cafe\u{301}"). In MemoryBackend both can coexist in one directory and list returns 2 entries.

casosBorde.titulo: join, parent, file_name, starts_with are segment-aware
casosBorde.cita: «`/`-separated» (l. 40) — a prefix test on raw strings would treat /ab as inside /a and rename_tree / remove_tree would touch a sibling
casosBorde.comportamiento: join accepts exactly one non-empty segment without '/', NUL, '.' or '..'. starts_with compares whole segments. parent(root) is None; file_name(root) is None.
casosBorde.verificable: root().join("a") == parse("/a"); join("a/b"), join(""), join("."), join("..") == Err(InvalidSegment{..}) (NUL -> ContainsNul); parse("/ab").starts_with(&parse("/a")) == false; parse("/a/b").starts_with(&parse("/a")) == true; every path starts_with root; parse("/a").parent() == Some(root); parse("/a/b").file_name() == Some("b").

casosBorde.titulo: DriveId validation
casosBorde.cita: «`kara+sftp://drive-id/…`» (l. 45) — the id is the URI authority, so it must need no escaping
casosBorde.comportamiento: scheme ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,15}$, name ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$. Anything else is rejected, never lower-cased or trimmed for the caller.
casosBorde.verificable: new("sftp","work-nas") Ok; new("SFTP","x"), new("","x"), new("1s","x"), new("s-3","x") -> InvalidScheme; new("sftp",""), ("sftp","-x"), ("sftp","x-"), ("sftp","Work"), ("sftp","a b"), ("sftp","a.b"), ("sftp", 64×"a") -> InvalidName; DriveId::new("sftp","x") != DriveId::new("s3","x").

casosBorde.titulo: Local URIs are byte-identical to kara_fs::uri::file_uri
casosBorde.cita: crates/kara-fs/src/uri.rs: «the thumbnail cache is keyed by the MD5 of this exact string […] Escape one byte differently from GLib or Qt and Kara silently stops seeing the thumbnails»
casosBorde.comportamiento: Same escape set, uppercase hex, raw OsStr bytes.
casosBorde.verificable: to_uri(Local("/tmp/a b#c%d?.txt")) == "file:///tmp/a%20b%23c%25d%3F.txt"; Local("/tmp/caf\u{e9}") -> "file:///tmp/caf%C3%A9"; Local(OsStr::from_bytes(b"/tmp/\xff")) -> "file:///tmp/%FF"; Local("/tmp/[x]{y}") -> "file:///tmp/%5Bx%5D%7By%7D"; Local("/tmp/l\nb") -> "file:///tmp/l%0Ab"; Local("/a&b=c;d,e+f!g'h(i)*j~k_l-m.n:o@p$q") is emitted unescaped after "file://". (The test pins these strings; kara-vfs must not depend on kara-fs.)

casosBorde.titulo: URI round trip is lossless
casosBorde.cita: «QML receives a `Location` as a string URI […] produced and parsed in Rust only. Breadcrumbs, Ctrl+L and bookmarks use it.» (l. 45-46)
casosBorde.comportamiento: from_uri(to_uri(l)?) == l for every valid Location.
casosBorde.verificable: Round trip holds for Local paths with spaces, '#', '%', '?', newline, non-UTF-8 byte 0xFF, and for Remote paths "/", "/a b/#%?[]", "/ünï/cødé", "/a\\b". to_uri(Remote{drive: sftp/work, path: "/home/ana/a b.txt"}) == "kara+sftp://work/home/ana/a%20b.txt"; to_uri(Remote{.., path: root}) == "kara+sftp://work/".

casosBorde.titulo: Remote root accepted with or without trailing slash
casosBorde.cita: «rutas de red y ubicaciones especiales […] también deben representarse como segmentos coherentes» (01-navegacion l. 17)
casosBorde.comportamiento: "kara+sftp://work" and "kara+sftp://work/" both parse to the drive root; to_uri always emits the slash form.
casosBorde.verificable: from_uri("kara+sftp://work") == from_uri("kara+sftp://work/") == Remote{drive: (sftp, work), path: root}.

casosBorde.titulo: from_uri rejects what Kara never produces
casosBorde.cita: «produced and parsed in Rust only» (l. 45-46) — a URI that is not Kara's canonical form is not silently reinterpreted
casosBorde.comportamiento: Strict parser, each failure typed.
casosBorde.verificable: "smb://h/x", "http://x", "sftp://h/x" (no kara+), "kara+://x/", "FILE:///x" -> UnsupportedScheme; "file://host/x" -> NonLocalFileHost{host:"host"}; "file:///a?b", "file:///a#b", "kara+sftp://w/a#b" -> QueryOrFragment; "file:///a%zz", "file:///a%4" -> InvalidPercentEncoding; "file:///a%00b", "kara+sftp://w/a%00" -> ContainsNul; "kara+sftp://w/%FF" -> Path(NotUtf8); "kara+sftp://w/a/../b" -> Path(DotSegment{..}); "kara+sftp://Bad_Name/" -> Drive(InvalidName{..}); "file:relative" and "file://" -> RelativeLocalPath or UnsupportedScheme, never Ok. to_uri(Local("rel/x")) and to_uri(Local("")) -> Err(RelativeLocalPath).

casosBorde.titulo: same_remote_drive and parent
casosBorde.cita: «Same remote drive and `server_side_copy`: `copy_within`.» (l. 115)
casosBorde.comportamiento: same_remote_drive is true only for two Remote locations whose DriveId (scheme AND name) is equal.
casosBorde.verificable: Remote(sftp/work,/a) vs Remote(sftp/work,/b) -> true; vs Remote(s3/work,/a) -> false; vs Remote(sftp/home,/a) -> false; Local vs Local -> false; Local vs Remote -> false. Remote(sftp/work,/a).parent() == Some(Remote(sftp/work, root)); Remote root .parent() == None; Local("/").parent() == None.

casosBorde.titulo: Errors are Send + Sync + 'static and keep their source
casosBorde.cita: «`BackendError { kind, path, source }`» (l. 87); CLAUDE.md «cada error se propaga o se reporta»
casosBorde.comportamiento: BackendError can cross the worker->UI boundary; std::error::Error::source() returns the wrapped error; Display contains the path.
casosBorde.verificable: A compile-time check `fn f<T: Send + Sync + 'static + std::error::Error>() {}` accepts BackendError and ConformanceError; BackendError::new(NotFound, Some(p)).with_source(io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::NotFound)).source().is_some(); format!("{e}") contains p.as_str().

casosBorde.titulo: Every error names the path it is about
casosBorde.cita: «el diálogo debe nombrar el archivo y el motivo en lenguaje llano» (05-operaciones l. 213)
casosBorde.comportamiento: Every Err from a Backend method that takes a path has path == Some(..): the argument for list/stat/open_read/begin_write/create_dir/remove/remove_tree; for rename: `from` when from is missing, `to` when to exists or to's parent is missing; for copy_within: same rule as rename; for remove_tree failing on a descendant: the descendant's path; for Cancelled: the argument path. path is None only for errors not about a path (none in this step: even Unavailable carries the argument path).
casosBorde.verificable: Covered by conformance case error_names_path on both MemoryBackend profiles, plus a MemoryBackend test with Fault{op: RemoveTree, after: 2, ..} whose error path is a descendant, not the root.

casosBorde.titulo: BackendError survives an io::Error round trip; Cancelled is never Interrupted
casosBorde.cita: «`kara-ops` maps it onto its existing `FailureKind` (`Unavailable` → `MediaGone`, so no infinite retry loop» (l. 89-90)
casosBorde.comportamiento: From<BackendError> for io::Error uses io kinds: NotFound->NotFound, AlreadyExists->AlreadyExists, PermissionDenied->PermissionDenied, NoSpace->StorageFull, Unavailable->NotConnected, AuthRequired->PermissionDenied, Unsupported->Unsupported, Cancelled->Other, Other->Other, with the BackendError as inner error. from_io recovers the original kind and path exactly. Cancelled MUST NOT become io::ErrorKind::Interrupted: std::io::copy, read_exact and write_all retry Interrupted silently, turning a cancel into a loop.
casosBorde.verificable: For each of the 9 kinds k: BackendError::from_io(io::Error::from(BackendError::new(k, Some(p))), None) has kind k and path Some(p). io::Error::from(BackendError::new(Cancelled, None)).kind() != Interrupted. A reader from MemoryBackend whose Read fault is FaultEffect::Fail(Unavailable) makes std::io::copy return an io::Error that from_io turns into kind Unavailable.

casosBorde.titulo: from_io mapping of foreign io::Errors
casosBorde.cita: «`Unavailable` (connection lost)» (l. 88) · «un medio extraíble que se desconecta a mitad debe detectarse y avisar, no colgar la operación indefinidamente» (05-operaciones l. 213)
casosBorde.comportamiento: Not wrapping a BackendError: NotFound->NotFound; AlreadyExists->AlreadyExists; PermissionDenied, ReadOnlyFilesystem->PermissionDenied; StorageFull, QuotaExceeded->NoSpace; ConnectionRefused, ConnectionReset, ConnectionAborted, NotConnected, BrokenPipe, TimedOut, HostUnreachable, NetworkUnreachable, NetworkDown, StaleNetworkFileHandle->Unavailable; raw errno EIO(5), ENXIO(6), ENODEV(19), ENOMEDIUM(123)->Unavailable (checked BEFORE the kind, since std maps some of them to Uncategorized); Unsupported->Unsupported; Interrupted and everything else->Other. The io::Error is kept as source.
casosBorde.verificable: Table-driven test over every row above using io::Error::from(kind) and io::Error::from_raw_os_error(n); from_io(io::Error::from_raw_os_error(28 /*ENOSPC*/), Some(&p)).kind == NoSpace and .path == Some(p); from_io(io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted), None).kind == Other.

casosBorde.titulo: No panics in kara-vfs, same scan as kara-fs
casosBorde.cita: «No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in `kara-vfs` or `kara-remote`, same rule and same scan as `kara-fs`.» (l. 91-92)
casosBorde.comportamiento: src/ (all modules, cfg(test) included, memory and conformance included) contains none of the forbidden macros/methods outside comment lines.
casosBorde.verificable: A test in crates/kara-vfs/tests/ reads every .rs under src/, skips lines whose trimmed start is "//", and finds no match of `\.unwrap\(|\.expect\(|panic!|unreachable!|todo!|unimplemented!|assert!|assert_eq!|assert_ne!|debug_assert`. Also `.unwrap_or`, `.unwrap_or_else`, `.unwrap_or_default` are allowed (they do not match `\.unwrap\(`).

casosBorde.titulo: Cancel is shared and idempotent
casosBorde.cita: «cancel mid-list and mid-transfer» (l. 159); kara-index walk.rs «La cancelación es cooperativa y se comprueba por entrada»
casosBorde.comportamiento: Clones share one flag; cancel() twice is fine; there is no un-cancel.
casosBorde.verificable: let a = Cancel::new(); let b = a.clone(); b.cancel(); b.cancel(); a.is_cancelled() == true; Cancel::default().is_cancelled() == false.

casosBorde.titulo: Backend is object safe, shareable, and its capabilities are constant
casosBorde.cita: «Blocking, `Send + Sync`.» (l. 50) · «`DriveRegistry` maps `DriveId` to `Arc<dyn Backend>`» (l. 130)
casosBorde.comportamiento: Arc<dyn Backend> is Send + Sync; capabilities() returns the same value for the lifetime of the backend, whatever operations or faults happen (disconnect included).
casosBorde.verificable: let b: Arc<dyn Backend> = Arc::new(MemoryBackend::posix_like()); moved into std::thread::spawn and used there; capabilities() equal before/after disconnect(), reconnect() and a full conformance run.

casosBorde.titulo: list: entry contract
casosBorde.cita: «list / stat round trip» (l. 154) · kara-fs listing.rs: «Entradas leídas, en el orden que dio el sistema de ficheros: sin ordenar. Ordenarlas es cosa de `kara_core::sort`»
casosBorde.comportamiento: No '.'/'..' entries; unsorted (callers must not rely on order); hidden ('.'-prefixed) included with is_hidden = true; name is the single segment as OsString and display == name; files: size Some(len); directories: size None; symlink entries: is_symlink true, kind resolved through the target, symlink_broken when the target is missing (broken -> kind File), size/times from the link itself; created/accessed None when the backend lacks them (MemoryBackend: None); type_label None; location None (until step 3); extra empty. Empty dir -> Ok(empty). Missing -> NotFound. A file -> Err(Other, source io NotADirectory). Root of an empty drive -> Ok(empty).
casosBorde.verificable: MemoryBackend tests in both profiles check each field listed; list(root) on a fresh MemoryBackend is Ok with 0 entries; list of "/f.txt" (a file) is Err with kind Other.

casosBorde.titulo: stat agrees with list; stat of root; stat under a file
casosBorde.cita: «list / stat round trip» (l. 154)
casosBorde.comportamiento: stat(dir.join(e.name)) equals the list entry e on every field. stat(root) is Ok, kind Directory, name "/" (as kara_fs::listing::describe does for "/"). stat of a path whose parent is a file is NotFound (ENOTDIR maps to NotFound for stat), not Other.
casosBorde.verificable: Equality on all FileEntry fields for every entry of a 5-entry dir in both profiles; stat(root).kind == Directory and name == "/"; stat("/f.txt/x") -> NotFound.

casosBorde.titulo: list is cancellable per entry and never returns a partial Ok
casosBorde.cita: «cancel mid-list» (l. 159) · CLAUDE.md «El listado de un directorio nunca bloquea la UI, ni con 100 k entradas ni con un volumen de red colgado»
casosBorde.comportamiento: cancel is checked before the first entry and at least once per entry; once observed, list returns Err(Cancelled) with path == dir. Never Ok with fewer entries.
casosBorde.verificable: Pre-cancelled token -> Err(Cancelled). MemoryBackend dir with 100_000 files and Fault{op: List, after: 10, effect: FaultEffect::Cancel(token), times: Some(1)} -> Err(Cancelled), and a counter wrapper shows at most 11 entries were produced (the fault cancels the shared token after 10 entries; the next check must see it).

casosBorde.titulo: open_read offsets and targets
casosBorde.cita: «Pausar y reanudar […] sin perder el progreso» (05-operaciones l. 33) — resuming is open_read(path, from)
casosBorde.comportamiento: from == 0 reads all; 0 < from < len reads the tail; from == len returns a reader at EOF; from > len -> Err(Other, source InvalidInput) at open time, not a short read; directory -> Err(Other, source IsADirectory); missing -> NotFound. Offset arithmetic never overflows (from = u64::MAX -> Err, not panic).
casosBorde.verificable: On a 10-byte file: from 0/4/10 read 10/6/0 bytes with the right content; from 11 and from u64::MAX -> Err. On a dir -> Err kind Other. On a missing path -> NotFound.

casosBorde.titulo: Write then read back: empty, small, multi-chunk
casosBorde.cita: «write → read back, empty file, file larger than one chunk» (l. 155)
casosBorde.comportamiento: finish commits exactly the bytes written, in order; size_hint is never enforced; an empty session commits an empty file.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance cases write_read_back, empty_file, multi_chunk_file, size_hint_is_only_a_hint pass on both profiles; stats().bytes_written increases by exactly the bytes written.

casosBorde.titulo: replace = false: refuse at begin, and again at finish
casosBorde.cita: «`replace = false` on an existing target fails with `AlreadyExists`» (l. 156) · «La opción por defecto […] debe ser la MENOS destructiva (no reemplazar automáticamente)» (05-operaciones l. 151)
casosBorde.comportamiento: begin_write(existing, false) fails immediately (no bytes sent). If the target appears while the session is open, finish fails with AlreadyExists, commits nothing, and the other writer's content stays.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance replace_false_existing and replace_false_race_at_finish; MemoryBackend snapshot after the failed finish equals the snapshot taken right after the competing finish.

casosBorde.titulo: replace = true never exposes a mix
casosBorde.cita: «A half-written destination is never visible under its final name.» (l. 82-83)
casosBorde.comportamiento: Until finish, the old content is what stat/open_read see. After finish, the new content. A reader opened before finish either reads the complete old content or returns an error; never old bytes followed by new bytes.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance replace_true. MemoryBackend (stricter): a reader opened before finish and read after finish returns the full OLD content.

casosBorde.titulo: Nothing visible before finish; abort and drop leave nothing behind
casosBorde.cita: «`fn abort(self: Box<Self>); // leave nothing behind`» (l. 76) · «Dropping a session without `finish` aborts it.» (l. 81-82) · «aborted or dropped `WriteSession` leaves nothing visible» (l. 157)
casosBorde.comportamiento: No entry with the final name and, for MemoryBackend, no node at all exists for an unfinished session; after abort() or drop the backend is as before begin_write and the session's bytes are released from the capacity count.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance invisible_before_finish, abort_leaves_nothing, drop_leaves_nothing. MemoryBackend: snapshot() before begin_write == snapshot() after abort/drop, and stats().open_sessions returns to its previous value; with set_capacity(Some(n)), a 3/4·n session that is aborted lets a second 3/4·n write succeed.

casosBorde.titulo: A failed write poisons the session
casosBorde.cita: «si el destino se queda sin espacio, el diálogo debe pausar y ofrecer reintentar/omitir/cancelar en vez de fallar en silencio» (05-operaciones l. 19)
casosBorde.comportamiento: When Write::write returns Err (NoSpace, Unavailable, injected), every later write returns Err and finish returns Err with the first error's kind; nothing is committed; a replace=true target keeps its old content.
casosBorde.verificable: MemoryBackend set_capacity(Some(100)), write 150 bytes: a write returns an io::Error whose from_io kind is NoSpace; finish -> Err(NoSpace); snapshot unchanged versus before begin_write; with replace=true on an existing file, its old content is intact.

casosBorde.titulo: Disconnect reaches open readers and sessions
casosBorde.cita: «un medio extraíble que se desconecta a mitad debe detectarse y avisar, no colgar la operación indefinidamente» (05-operaciones l. 213)
casosBorde.comportamiento: After MemoryBackend::disconnect(): every Backend method returns Unavailable with the argument path; an already-open reader's next read returns an io::Error mapping to Unavailable; an open session's write/finish return Unavailable and commit nothing. After reconnect(), committed data is still there and the unfinished file is not.
casosBorde.verificable: Sequence begin_write+write, open_read, disconnect, read -> Unavailable, finish -> Unavailable, reconnect: snapshot equals the pre-session snapshot; list/stat work again.

casosBorde.titulo: A directory is never replaced by a file
casosBorde.cita: «conflicto entre archivo y carpeta con el mismo nombre debe tratarse aparte (no sobrescribir una carpeta con un archivo sin aviso explícito)» (05-operaciones l. 151)
casosBorde.comportamiento: begin_write on an existing directory (or a DirMarker / implicit prefix in the object profile) fails with AlreadyExists for replace=false AND replace=true; the directory and its children are untouched.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance write_onto_directory on both profiles; MemoryBackend snapshot unchanged.

casosBorde.titulo: Missing parent depends on real_directories
casosBorde.cita: «`real_directories` | yes | no (prefixes) | «Nueva carpeta» creates a `key/` marker» (l. 104)
casosBorde.comportamiento: real_directories = true: create_dir, begin_write and rename into a missing parent -> NotFound (path = the requested path), nothing created; create_dir is not recursive. real_directories = false: begin_write under a missing prefix succeeds and every ancestor prefix lists as a Directory; create_dir creates a DirMarker only for the requested path.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance missing_parent on both profiles; MemoryBackend object profile: after begin_write("/x/y/z")+finish, list(root) contains "x" as Directory and snapshot has no DirMarker for /x or /x/y.

casosBorde.titulo: Concurrent sessions do not share temporary state
casosBorde.cita: «SFTP writes to a temporary name and renames» (l. 80-81) — two sessions on one target must not write into one temp file
casosBorde.comportamiento: Two sessions on the same target are independent: with replace=true the final content is exactly one session's bytes; with replace=false the second finish is AlreadyExists.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance concurrent_sessions_same_target and replace_false_race_at_finish; MemoryBackend stats().open_sessions == 2 while both are open.

casosBorde.titulo: abort reports its own failure; Drop never panics
casosBorde.cita: CLAUDE.md: «Cada syscall devuelve `Result` y cada error se propaga o se reporta» (dec_02)
casosBorde.comportamiento: abort() returns Err when cleanup fails (MemoryBackend: Unavailable when disconnected; the session's bytes are still released so nothing becomes visible). Drop calls the same cleanup and ignores only its Result.
casosBorde.verificable: disconnect(), then abort() of an open session -> Err(Unavailable); after reconnect(), snapshot shows nothing from it. Dropping a session while disconnected does not panic.

casosBorde.titulo: create_dir is exact and never merges
casosBorde.cita: «Nueva carpeta» (l. 104) · «mover, copiar, renombrar y crear entran en la pila de deshacer» (CLAUDE.md) — create must be undoable, so it must report whether it created anything
casosBorde.comportamiento: create_dir on an existing directory or file -> AlreadyExists, nothing changed (never Ok on an existing directory: undo would then delete something Kara did not create). Object profile: create_dir writes a DirMarker; list(dir) is Ok and empty (the marker is never an entry, no entry named ""); stat(dir) is Directory.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance create_dir, create_dir_existing; MemoryBackend object profile: snapshot().nodes[dir] == DirMarker and list(dir).entries.is_empty().

casosBorde.titulo: rename never overwrites
casosBorde.cita: «no reemplazar automáticamente» (05-operaciones l. 151) — POSIX rename(2) replaces silently; the trait forbids it
casosBorde.comportamiento: If `to` exists (file, dir, marker or implicit prefix) -> AlreadyExists with path == to; both untouched. LocalBackend (step 2) will need renameat2(NOREPLACE), as kara-fs trash already does.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance rename_never_overwrites on both profiles; MemoryBackend snapshot unchanged after the Err.

casosBorde.titulo: rename(x, x) is a no-op
casosBorde.cita: «mover a la misma carpeta (origen == destino) no es conflicto sino no-op» (05-operaciones l. 151)
casosBorde.comportamiento: from == to -> Ok(()) without touching anything (checked before the exists test, so it is not AlreadyExists).
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance rename_same_is_noop; MemoryBackend snapshot unchanged.

casosBorde.titulo: rename refuses impossible targets
casosBorde.cita: «Reversibilidad por defecto» (00-filosofia l. 12) — moving a folder into itself or renaming the drive root cannot be undone
casosBorde.comportamiento: to.starts_with(from) with to != from -> Err(Other, source InvalidInput), no change. from == root or to == root -> Err(Other, InvalidInput). from missing -> NotFound(path = from).
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance rename_into_own_subtree; MemoryBackend: rename(root, "/x") and rename("/x", root) -> Err kind Other, snapshot unchanged; rename(missing, "/y") -> NotFound with path == missing.

casosBorde.titulo: Non-atomic rename never loses data
casosBorde.cita: «`atomic_rename` | yes | no (copy+delete)» (l. 102) · «The source is never deleted if the copy failed» (l. 119-120)
casosBorde.comportamiento: With atomic_rename = false, rename of a file or tree is per-object copy then delete-of-that-object-only-after-its-copy-succeeded. On any failure midway it returns Err and every original object exists, with its original content, under `from` or under `to` (possibly both); none is lost.
casosBorde.verificable: MemoryBackend object profile, tree of 10 files, Fault{op: Rename, after: k, effect: Fail(Unavailable), times: Some(1)} for each k in 0..10: Err returned, and for every original file f, read(from/f) or read(to/f) equals its original content. With atomic_rename = true (posix profile) the same fault leaves the tree entirely under `from`.

casosBorde.titulo: remove: file or empty dir only
casosBorde.cita: «fn remove(&self, path: &RemotePath) -> Result<(), BackendError>; // file or empty dir» (l. 67)
casosBorde.comportamiento: Non-empty dir -> Err(Other, source DirectoryNotEmpty), nothing removed. Missing -> NotFound. Root -> Err(Other, InvalidInput). A symlink is removed as a link (target untouched). Object profile: removing an empty marker-only dir removes the marker.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance remove_file_and_empty_dir, remove_nonempty_dir, remove_missing; MemoryBackend remove(root) -> Err, snapshot unchanged.

casosBorde.titulo: remove_tree: refuses the root, cancellable, stops at the first failure
casosBorde.cita: «carpetas grandes deben mostrar diálogo de progreso y poder cancelarse» (05-operaciones l. 255) · «Reversibilidad por defecto» (00-filosofia l. 12)
casosBorde.comportamiento: remove_tree(root) -> Err(Other, InvalidInput) and removes nothing (wiping a whole drive by accident is the one thing a backend refuses). Deletes deepest first; checks cancel before every entry; on Cancelled or on a failure returns Err with the path of the entry being processed (Cancelled: the argument path); what was already removed stays removed (not transactional, documented) and nothing else is attempted. On a file it removes the file. Missing -> NotFound.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance remove_tree, remove_tree_precancelled; MemoryBackend: remove_tree(root) -> Err, snapshot unchanged; Fault{op: RemoveTree, after: 3, effect: Cancel(token)} on a 10-file tree -> Err(Cancelled) and exactly 3 files are gone; Fault{op: RemoveTree, after: 3, effect: Fail(PermissionDenied)} -> Err(PermissionDenied) whose path is a descendant and 3 files are gone.

casosBorde.titulo: Symlinks are never followed by destructive operations
casosBorde.cita: «`symlinks` | yes | no» (l. 106) · «Reversibilidad por defecto» (00-filosofia l. 12) — following a link would delete data outside the selection
casosBorde.comportamiento: remove and remove_tree remove the link, never descend into or delete its target; rename moves the link; open_read follows the link (reads the target); list reports links per cb_18. MemoryBackend::create_symlink returns Unsupported without the capability.
casosBorde.verificable: MemoryBackend posix profile: /t/keep.txt and /d/l -> "/t"; remove_tree("/d") Ok and /t/keep.txt still readable; a broken link lists with symlink_broken = true and remove() Ok; object profile create_symlink -> Unsupported.

casosBorde.titulo: Implicit directories of the object profile
casosBorde.cita: «`real_directories` | yes | no (prefixes)» (l. 104) · «S3 is deferred, but the contract is still checked against it […] so it must not be shaped around SFTP alone» (l. 12-14)
casosBorde.comportamiento: With real_directories = false a directory exists iff it has a DirMarker or at least one descendant object. Removing the last descendant of an unmarked prefix makes it vanish from list(parent) and stat -> NotFound. Listing a prefix that has neither -> NotFound (not an empty Ok), except root.
casosBorde.verificable: Conformance implicit_directories passes on the object profile and is Skipped{because: "real_directories=true"} on posix; MemoryBackend: begin_write("/p/f")+finish, remove("/p/f"), then stat("/p") -> NotFound and list("/p") -> NotFound.

casosBorde.titulo: copy_within: only when declared, moves no bytes through the client
casosBorde.cita: «/// Only called if `capabilities().server_side_copy`.» (l. 70) · «Copy inside the drive moves no bytes» (l. 103)
casosBorde.comportamiento: Without server_side_copy: Err(Unsupported) and no change (it is still never a panic). With it: copies a FILE; target exists -> AlreadyExists (no replace flag); source directory -> Unsupported (tree copies are composed by kara-ops); missing source -> NotFound(path = from).
casosBorde.verificable: MemoryBackend posix profile copy_within -> Unsupported, snapshot unchanged. Object profile: copy of a 3 MiB file succeeds and stats().bytes_read and bytes_written are unchanged by it; conformance copy_within passes.

casosBorde.titulo: Every error kind is reachable, and a failed mutation changes nothing
casosBorde.cita: «every error kind reachable, and only declared capabilities are exercised» (l. 160)
casosBorde.comportamiento: MemoryBackend produces each of the 9 kinds through a real path: NotFound, AlreadyExists (natural), PermissionDenied / AuthRequired / Other (Fault), NoSpace (set_capacity), Unavailable (disconnect), Unsupported (copy_within without capability, create_symlink), Cancelled (Cancel). A Fault on a mutating op (create_dir, rename on the posix profile, remove, begin_write, finish) leaves the snapshot unchanged.
casosBorde.verificable: One test per kind named cb_42_<kind>; each mutating-op fault test compares snapshots before/after.

casosBorde.titulo: The suite refuses a dirty or missing scratch and stays inside it
casosBorde.cita: «SFTP and S3 run it against a real server» (l. 162-163) — the suite will run on real servers, so it must not be able to delete what it did not create
casosBorde.comportamiento: run(): scratch missing -> Err(ScratchUnreachable(NotFound)); scratch is a file -> Err(ScratchNotDirectory); scratch has any entry -> Err(ScratchNotEmpty{entries}) — in all three cases it calls no mutating method. It never calls a mutating method on a path that is not strictly under scratch. On success scratch is empty again.
casosBorde.verificable: A test-side spy Backend wrapper records every path passed to create_dir/begin_write/rename/remove/remove_tree/copy_within: all start_with scratch and none equals scratch; with a pre-existing entry, the spy records zero mutating calls and the entry survives; after a successful run list(scratch) is empty.

casosBorde.titulo: The suite only exercises declared capabilities
casosBorde.cita: «only declared capabilities are exercised» (l. 160)
casosBorde.comportamiento: copy_within is never called when !server_side_copy; implicit_directories is skipped when real_directories. A skipped case states the capability condition in `because`.
casosBorde.verificable: Spy wrapper over MemoryBackend::posix_like(): copy_within call count == 0, report has copy_within: Skipped{because: "server_side_copy=false"} and implicit_directories: Skipped{because: "real_directories=true"}. Over object_store_like(): neither is skipped and no case is Skipped.

casosBorde.titulo: The suite catches broken backends (a passing suite must mean something)
casosBorde.cita: CLAUDE.md: «A passing test proves little: break the invariant on purpose once and see it fail»
casosBorde.comportamiento: Running the suite on deliberately broken wrappers yields Failed (never a panic, never Passed) for the matching case.
casosBorde.verificable: Test-side wrappers over MemoryBackend, each breaking one rule: (a) rename that removes `to` first then renames -> rename_never_overwrites Failed; (b) begin_write ignoring replace=false -> replace_false_existing Failed; (c) WriteSession whose abort/drop commits -> abort_leaves_nothing and drop_leaves_nothing Failed; (d) list that ignores Cancel -> list_precancelled Failed; (e) WriteSession that commits on every write -> invisible_before_finish Failed; (f) remove that removes non-empty dirs -> remove_nonempty_dir Failed; (g) errors with path None -> error_names_path Failed. report.is_success() == false in each, and run() returns Ok(report) (the suite itself does not error).

casosBorde.titulo: Both MemoryBackend profiles pass the whole suite
casosBorde.cita: «`MemoryBackend` and `LocalBackend` run it in CI.» (l. 162) · «must not be shaped around SFTP alone» (l. 14)
casosBorde.comportamiento: posix_like() and object_store_like() pass every non-skipped case.
casosBorde.verificable: run(&MemoryBackend::posix_like(), &scratch) and run(&MemoryBackend::object_store_like(), &scratch) after create_dir(scratch): Ok(report) with is_success() and report.cases ids == CASE_IDS in order.

casosBorde.titulo: Backend calls never block forever and never need a runtime
casosBorde.cita: «Blocking, `Send + Sync`. […] an async trait would force a runtime on every caller» (l. 50-52) · CLAUDE.md «Nada debe bloquear la UI, ni con 100k entradas ni con un volumen colgado»
casosBorde.comportamiento: MemoryBackend never waits: every method returns without sleeping or blocking on a condition (a disconnected backend answers Unavailable at once). Concurrent use from several threads is safe: list from one thread while another writes.
casosBorde.verificable: 8 threads × 200 iterations of begin_write/finish/list/stat/remove on distinct names in one Arc<dyn Backend> finish with no error other than expected ones and a final list consistent with the operations; a disconnected backend answers 10_000 stat calls in well under 1 s (release-independent bound: 2 s).

casosBorde.titulo: Layering and features
casosBorde.cita: «kara-ui → kara-ops → { kara-fs, kara-remote, kara-index } → kara-vfs → kara-core» (l. 19) · «the conformance suite (feature `conformance`). No protocol code.» (l. 24)
casosBorde.comportamiento: kara-vfs normal deps: kara-core, thiserror, percent-encoding only. default features empty; memory and conformance compile only when enabled; plain `cargo test -p kara-vfs` runs the suite thanks to the self dev-dependency (dec_06). No existing crate depends on kara-vfs yet.
casosBorde.verificable: `cargo tree -p kara-vfs -e normal --depth 1` lists exactly kara-core, percent-encoding, thiserror; `cargo check -p kara-vfs --no-default-features` succeeds; `cargo test -p kara-vfs -- --list` includes the conformance tests; `grep -rn kara-vfs crates/*/Cargo.toml` matches only crates/kara-vfs/Cargo.toml.

criteriosDeAceptacion.criterio: `cargo test -p kara-vfs` passes: 0 failed, 0 ignored. Workspace `cargo test` is still green and the sha256 of every file in crates/kara-fs/tests/ is unchanged.
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0 for the whole workspace, kara-vfs included, without new crate-wide `allow`s.

The no-panic scan of cb_15 exists as a test in crates/kara-vfs/tests/ and passes; `grep -rnE '\.unwrap\(|\.expect\(|panic!|unreachable!|todo!|unimplemented!|assert' crates/kara-vfs/src/` prints nothing outside comment lines.

Every signature in apiPublica exists with the exact name, parameter types and return type: a compile-only test coerces each function/method to a fn pointer of the stated type and each trait to `dyn` (Arc<dyn Backend>, Box<dyn WriteSession>).
Each of cb_01…cb_48 has at least one test whose name contains its id, and each test checks observable state (snapshot, list, read-back), not only the variant of a Result.
Every test that expects a failed mutating operation also asserts MemorySnapshot equality before/after (or, for cb_36/cb_38, the exact documented partial state).

conformance::run on MemoryBackend::posix_like() and ::object_store_like() returns Ok(report) with report.is_success(), and report.cases ids equal CASE_IDS in order (39 ids, exactly those of casosDeConformidad).
At least the 7 broken-backend wrappers of cb_45 make the matching case Failed; none makes run() panic or return Err.
Dependencies per cb_48; `git diff --stat` touches only crates/kara-vfs/**, the root Cargo.toml (members + workspace.dependencies) and Cargo.lock.
Code, identifiers, comments and doc comments in kara-vfs are in English; the crate-level doc names this contract's slug and links docs/remote-backends.md.
`cargo doc -p kara-vfs --features memory,conformance --no-deps` emits no warnings (broken intra-doc links included).

riesgosDeImplementacionPlausiblePeroInco: Resolving '..' lexically in RemotePath::parse instead of rejecting it (cb_02): gives S3 keys filesystem semantics the doc forbids.
String prefix test for starts_with: /ab counted as inside /a, so rename-into-self and remove_tree checks touch siblings (cb_04, cb_35).
Percent-encoding the local path through to_string_lossy, or with a different escape set than kara-fs uri.rs: breaks the shared thumbnail cache and non-UTF-8 round trips (cb_06, cb_07).
Mapping Cancelled to io::ErrorKind::Interrupted: io::copy and write_all retry Interrupted forever (cb_13).
Losing the kind through io::Error (from_io that only looks at io::ErrorKind): a disconnect mid-transfer becomes Other and kara-ops retries it in a loop (cb_13, cb_27).
Returning Ok with the entries read so far when list is cancelled (cb_20).
Committing on Drop, or writing straight to the final name and deleting on abort (visible half-written file in between) (cb_24, cb_25).
Checking replace=false only at begin_write, so a racing writer's file is overwritten at finish (cb_23).
Letting finish succeed after a failed write (session not poisoned): a truncated file appears under its final name (cb_26).
Using a POSIX-style rename that replaces an existing target (cb_33), or treating rename(x, x) as AlreadyExists (cb_34).
create_dir returning Ok on an existing directory: undo would later delete a folder Kara did not create (cb_32).

Object profile: deleting the source object before its copy is confirmed in a non-atomic rename (cb_36); keeping implicit directories alive after their last object is gone, or returning an empty Ok for a missing prefix (cb_40).
remove_tree accepting the drive root, or following a symlink into its target (cb_38, cb_39).
A conformance suite built on assert!: violates the no-panic rule and turns a broken backend into a test-harness crash instead of a report (cb_15, cb_45).
A suite that cleans up with remove_tree(scratch) or touches paths outside scratch: on a real server it would delete user data (cb_43).
Exercising copy_within on a backend that does not declare server_side_copy (cb_44).
Counting copy_within bytes in MemoryStats, which would make «moves no bytes» untestable (cb_41).
Holding the MemoryBackend Mutex across a returned reader/session, deadlocking concurrent callers (cb_47).
